local.title: The Brevard County jail
local.lead: Brevard County owns the Jail Complex in Cocoa, and the Sheriff runs it. Everyone arrested anywhere in the county — by deputies or by any of the 16 cities’ police — is taken there. It is paid for out of the county’s General Fund.

facts.v: 1,849 rated beds — a main jail that opened in 1986 with 386 beds, plus four tent housing structures, an annex, and a mental health and medical unit. It “routinely houses over 1,600 inmates daily.”

src.label: Brevard County Sheriff’s Office — Jail Complex

facts.v: In February 2023 the jail averaged 1,431 people a day. 1,242 of them — 86.8% — had not been convicted: 1,073 awaiting trial on felonies and 169 on misdemeanors. That is the most recent count found (Docket #5).

src.label: Florida Dept. of Corrections — County Detention Facilities, Feb. 2023

facts.v: $66,553,297 is proposed to run the jail in FY2026-27, up from $61,596,061 this past year — inside the Sheriff’s $220,439,187 budget. That is roughly $99 per bed per day. Jail food and medical care alone was $13,402,347 in the Sheriff’s FY2025-26 request.

A year ago the Sheriff counted 577 open repair and replacement work orders at the jail. At the county’s September 2026 budget hearing he described a 40-year-old jail with over 690 open work orders and asked for at least $3.5 million a year for repairs.

Already offered, by request and with classification approval: GED prep and testing; barber licensing, ServSafe manager certification, OSHA 30, traffic flagger, sewing, garment printing, floor care, canine training (Paws & Stripes); the Sheriff’s Farm; AA, NA, parenting, finance, and a veterans program (SAVE). The Sheriff says the trade programs give “a practical skill, which will lead to certification.”

The Sheriff’s Farm started in the 1980s as an alternative to a prison sentence. In 2017 it farmed 13 acres, with one potato crop expected to yield 35,000–40,000 pounds for the jail kitchen. Jail crews also keep up the lawns of 28 county properties (362 acres), which the Sheriff values at $265,000 a year.
The jail’s budget lists $48,000 a year from Eastern Florida State College as a “Veterinary Technician” reimbursement. What that program teaches, and to whom, isn’t described (Docket #6).
The local circuit runs a voluntary drug court: 12 to 18 months of treatment, and the felony charge is dismissed on completion. It also runs a veterans treatment court.
The Sheriff’s prisoner transport program “transports arrestees from locations throughout the county to the Brevard County Jail.”
